faqs.q: What are Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes used for?
faqs.a: Seamless chrome-moly tubes for superheaters, reheaters and high-temperature exchangers, to ASTM A213 T-grades (T11, T22, T91 and others), A209 and EN 10216-2. The grade sets the temperature: higher chrome and molybdenum carry the tube further into the creep range. It is listed in 10 sizes, 38.1–76.2 mm outside diameter.

faqs.q: How do I read an Indus part number for Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes, such as IH-TF-AB-AL-0381-419?
faqs.a: Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes part numbers begin with IH-TF-AB-AL and then give the outside diameter in tenths of a millimetre and the wall thickness in hundredths of a millimetre. IH-TF-AB-AL-0381-419 is 38.10 mm outside diameter by 4.19 mm wall, and IH-TF-AB-AL-0762-419 is the largest size listed. Quote the full part number, or the standard, grade, OD and wall.

faqs.q: What sizes do Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes come in?
faqs.a: Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes are listed in 10 sizes, 38.1–76.2 mm outside diameter, each with its own Indus part number, for example IH-TF-AB-AL-0381-419 and IH-TF-AB-AL-0762-419. The table includes 38.10 mm OD by 4.19 mm wall and 76.20 mm OD by 4.19 mm wall.

faqs.q: What do I need to send to order Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes to the right size and grade?
faqs.a: For Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes, quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the standard and grade, the outside diameter and wall (BWG or millimetres, minimum or average wall), the length and the quantity. We quote with the mill certificates and the inspection you need.

faqs.q: What is the maximum service temperature of Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes?
faqs.a: For Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes, max service temperature (indicative): 13CrMo4-5 class about 550–560 °C; 10CrMo9-10 class about 575–580 °C; 9Cr-1Mo-V (T91) class up to about 650 °C.

faqs.q: What tests and certificates come with Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes?
faqs.a: For Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes, testing follows the governing standard: A213: heat and product analysis, tensile, hardness, flattening, flaring, hydrostatic or NDT (E213/E309/E570). Mills recommend combining two NDT methods (UT to E213 and eddy current to E309) for A209/A213. Mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1 on request; third-party inspection by arrangement. Say on the enquiry which tests and inspection your project needs.

faqs.q: Which materials and grades are Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes available in?
faqs.a: Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes are available in these grades: A213 T5/T9/T11/T12/T22/T91; A209 T1/T1a/T1b; 16Mo3; 13CrMo4-5; 10CrMo9-10; 15CrMoG; 12Cr1MoVG.

faqs.q: Which standards apply to Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes?
faqs.a: Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes are made to ASTM A213 / SA-213, ASTM A209 / SA-209, ASTM A1016, EN 10216-2, DIN 17175 (superseded by EN 10216-2), GB/T 5310, JIS G3462, BS 3059. Tell us the standard and grade on your enquiry; equivalent grades in other standards are indicative and are checked against each tender.

faqs.q: What do Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes connect to or fit with?
faqs.a: For Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes, tubes are rolled or welded into tube sheets or headers and carried on baffles or supports, so the outside diameter and wall must match the tube sheet drilling. Related ranges are the [Precision & Mechanical Tubes](/c/precision-mechanical-tubes) and [Stainless Steel Tubes & Pipes](/c/stainless-steel-heat-exchanger-tubes) shelves.

faqs.q: How should Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes be inspected on receipt and stored?
faqs.a: Check Alloy Steel Boiler and Superheater Tubes on receipt against the order: outside diameter, wall, length, marking and the certificate heat numbers, and keep the ends capped until installation. Handle and store the material so the surface is not scratched or dented. The [Reading a mill test certificate to EN 10204 3.1](/blog/en-10204-3-1-mill-test-certificate) explains how to read the certificate.
